PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep cloud creation context for New Session
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

A cloud session's connection-bound backend and remote execution folder cannot create another cloud session. Inheriting them caused New Session to fall back to the previous local workspace.

- Add an optional provider-owned creation target, separate from the existing session's execution identity.
- Have cloud sandbox providers supply the known GitHub repository and the logical Cloud creation provider.
- Keep creation availability checks and ordinary harness fallback behavior. The shared inheritance helper also covers voice and archive-driven creation.
- Document the small provider contract and cover cached repository URLs, host repository metadata, desktop/web creators, unavailable targets, and the New Session action.

No session identity rewriting, host provisioning changes, or new protocol requests.

## How to test

Open a repository-backed cloud session after using a local workspace. Invoke New Session: the new draft should retain the repository and Cloud target. Confirm ordinary local/remote New Session and hidden-provider fallback still work.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newSessionAction.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceBridge.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts` — 724 passing, 2 pre-existing pending.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD -- "*.ts" | xargs npm run eslint --` — passed on the combined validation branch.

Not run: manual interaction with a live cloud sandbox.

## Review follow-up

Explicit source-harness overrides (such as leaving a Dev Container) do not query a different provider with the container session resource. The five-file test command above now passes 725 tests with 2 pre-existing pending after adding that regression. Final combined type, layer and lint checks passed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path and subscription behavior are explicit in repository code, and grouped-list actions demonstrably choose inactive sessions. Exact transcript sizes and remote latency vary, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: agent-host session/chat subscriptions, including a full default-chat snapshot and its deserialized objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added work is one remote Session subscription plus a ref-counted Chat subscription per previously inactive source session selected by a New Session gesture; the transferred and retained chat snapshot grows with that source conversation's transcript size and remains subscribed for the 30-second idle window.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: unnecessary remote traffic, transcript deserialization/GC pressure, and contention that can delay the newly opened composer or the chat the user is actually viewing
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Section/environment New Session actions used the already-present ISession workspace and provider fields and did not resolve the source through BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.getSessionByResource, so choosing an inactive cloud row did not restore or hydrate that source session.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: CloudSandboxSessionsProvider.getNewSessionTarget now calls getSessionByResource merely to read cached workspace metadata. That base lookup is an opening/query path: it calls _keepSessionStateAlive with hydrateDraft=true, acquiring a Session subscription and then draft agent/model hydration subscriptions for the default Chat.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 44 newly routes creation-target lookup through getSessionByResource; before this PR no creation-target lookup existed and openNewSessionLike directly reused session.workspace/providerId.
Findings.Title: Avoid hydrating the source chat when deriving the creation target
Findings.Impact: Clicking New Session on a repository/workspace/environment group whose chosen cloud sandbox session is not currently visible can restore and download that old session's default chat. Large historical chats therefore consume remote bandwidth and frontend allocation while the user is moving to a fresh session.
Findings.Evidence: The added line calls getSessionByResource. BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.getSessionByResource invokes _keepSessionStateAlive(cached.sessionId); _ensureSessionStateSubscription then opens StateComponents.Session and, because hydrateDraft defaults true, _ensureDraftHydration opens StateComponents.Chat for draft agent/model. The base provider explicitly documents that a chat snapshot carries the whole transcript and that passive observers must pass false because fetching unopened chats delays the chat being viewed. sessionsViewActions now reaches this path after selecting a source from grouped list sessions, which need not be a visible/pinned session.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve the target from a side-effect-free cached-session lookup, or add/use a non-hydrating getSessionByResource mode (equivalent to the existing passive-observer hydrateDraft=false behavior) so reading repository metadata never opens Session/Chat subscriptions.

Scenarios.Scenario: New Session from an active cloud sandbox via the main action, voice bridge, or archive transition
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The gesture synchronously derives the inherited target and checks logical-provider availability before opening the new draft; cloud provisioning/request work remains downstream of the selected provider. For an already visible active source, its agent-host state subscription is normally pinned, so the added lookup usually shares existing state rather than adding a round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reference-counted agent-host Session/Chat subscription used by getSessionByResource and draft hydration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one source Session and one default Chat subscription per gesture; normally shared for the active visible session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Target inheritance read activeSession.workspace/provider fields without calling getSessionByResource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The target lookup itself does not await hydration, but a cold subscription competes for transport/deserialization resources while the new composer opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same New Session workflow already performed one provider creation; the PR changes the intended provider/workspace selection for cloud sources rather than adding a second creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation is on the workflow critical path according to the existing openNewSession flow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source session and one target derivation per user gesture; provider availability scans the small registered logical-provider set once when the alternate target is available.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Target derivation is synchronous. Existing agent-host subscriptions are reference-counted; new-session creation follows the existing service/provider sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm visible sessions already have a pinned Session subscription and typically cached workspace/git metadata. On a cold provider cache, getSessionByResource can invoke the provider's coalesced _ensureSessionCache refresh, but active sessions are normally already represented.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the target helper, provider lookup, and subscription/ref-count behavior are explicit; whether a particular active source is already warm depends on visibility.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Active-session invocations are generally warm, so the incremental cost is often negligible; latency depends on connection state and transcript size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for active-session gestures because the subscription is normally already pinned and the operation remains one-per-gesture.

Scenarios.Scenario: New Session from a workspace/repository/environment section using an inactive cloud sandbox as the source
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After opening the fresh draft, openNewSessionLike derives the source target and applies it to the new view. The derivation synchronously calls the cloud backend; remote subscriptions it starts are asynchronous but contend with the newly opened session and remain alive for 30 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to agent-host Session state and the default Chat snapshot for draft agent/model hydration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Session channel plus one effective ref-counted Chat channel for the chosen inactive source; transcript bytes scale with that single conversation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The section action directly reused the ISession workspace/provider data and did not open source-session state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by target derivation, but downloads/deserializes an unrelated historical chat while the new composer/session is progressing, causing transport, CPU, GC, and retained-memory contention.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold listSessions refresh if the backend adapter cache has not initialized
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced refresh per provider because in-flight/retry guards suppress duplicates
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The section action did not call getSessionByResource, though normal session-list loading commonly initialized this cache earlier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget and generally already completed when a section can display the source; not the primary regression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one selected source per command after section grouping/deduplication. Payload cost scales with the selected source's default-chat transcript size, not with every row in the section.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One source lookup per command. Session and Chat subscriptions are reference-counted, but an inactive list-only source has no visible-session pin and can therefore create a new remote subscription alongside new-session work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session summary/workspace is already present to render the section, but getSessionByResource upgrades that cached adapter into live Session state and hydrateDraft=true Chat state. The subscription and hydrated objects remain until the 30-second idle timer expires; repeated gestures reset the timer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: base-provider comments explicitly state passive reads must avoid hydrateDraft because Chat snapshots carry the whole transcript, and grouped-list sources need not be visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost is small for short/warm chats but can be substantial for long remote histories or a sleeping/slow host.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager remote work: deriving repository metadata from an inactive source unnecessarily restores/hydrates its chat.

Scenarios.Scenario: New Session when the provider-owned cloud creation target is unavailable
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The helper first resolves the provider-owned target and scans logical providers for availability; if unavailable it performs the existing fallback availability check for the execution workspace before continuing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Source Session/default Chat subscription during alternate-target derivation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the fallback workspace/provider availability scan ran; no source hydration occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background contention rather than an awaited target check; covered by the submitted finding.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source session; up to two scans over registered logical providers and their advertised session types per gesture.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All availability checks are synchronous and serial. Any source-state subscription started by getSessionByResource is asynchronous and reference-counted.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider/session metadata is cached, but the cloud lookup can still create/reset the 30-second live state subscription. There is no negative cache for an unavailable creation target; invocation frequency is bounded by explicit gestures.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra source subscription and two synchronous availability scans.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count is small and resolveWorkspace/getSessionTypes are synchronous for the relevant GitHub/agent-host URI schemes, so the second scan is unlikely to be user-visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: The hydration is covered by the finding; the additional bounded provider scan is not independently reportable.

Scenarios.Scenario: New Session from ordinary local/remote providers that do not implement a provider-owned creation target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The helper performs a map lookup for the provider and then the same workspace/session-type availability enumeration used before the PR.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One provider lookup and one logical-provider scan per explicit gesture.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous only; no new subprocess, filesystem, IPC, database, or network operation is reached when getNewSessionTarget is absent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider registry lookup is a warm Map read. Workspace resolution constructs lightweight descriptors from existing configuration/URI data for the relevant providers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: optional dispatch returns without provider work, and inspected resolveWorkspace implementations are synchronous.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom future providers could implement more expensive synchronous logic, but that is not introduced by this diff and is not evidence for a current regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the added optional lookup is constant-time and the existing availability work remains bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 12 changed files and all diff pages. One performance regression was submitted: cloud creation-target resolution uses an opening/hydrating session lookup, causing unnecessary remote Session/Chat state work for inactive grouped-list sources. Other added work is bounded to explicit gestures, synchronous provider-map/availability checks, or normally shared warm subscriptions; no regression-fix learning signal was present.
